sentence: An implementer who follows 'observation.agentWait is never non-null' builds a check that passes when the field is absent; the document never says what an absent agentWait means or that absence must fail, so calling this wrong needs an added assumption about an unstated edge case.
evidence: document.md:181 'Pass: observation.agentWait is never non-null (a non-null value means the worker is parked on a prompt only a person can answer...)'; no line in document.md defines absent or null values.

sentence: An implementer who follows the text as written runs the P0 smoke runs and finds AC-0.4 step 3 unsatisfiable: step 3 requires the report path to be the WC-4 contract path, line 194 says the contract arrives only in P1 and that only step 4 uses the existing report file, and line 91 gives troubleshoot's report as REPORT.md; so the acceptance criterion 'steps 1-3 and 5-7 pass' cannot pass for troubleshoot, which is wrong because it forces a false P0 failure that 'reopens section 1'.
evidence: document.md:182 'its report path is the WC-4 contract path'; document.md:194 'steps 1-3 and 5-7 pass; step 4 uses the command's existing report file, since the contract arrives in P1'; document.md:62 WC-4 contract; document.md:91 troubleshoot 'REPORT.md (report_path)'; document.md:158 P0 runs troubleshoot.

sentence: WC-4 fixes the contract in the directory the coordinator passed and WC-6 requires each run to use a fresh output directory; these agree when the coordinator passes a new directory on retry, and the document never states what a retry brief passes, so a conflict appears only under an added assumption that the retry repeats the same directory.
evidence: document.md:62 WC-4 '<output-dir>/return-contract.yaml, where <output-dir> is the directory the coordinator passed'; document.md:64 WC-6 'writes each run into a fresh output directory'; document.md:73 section 2.3 says nothing about retry directories.

sentence: The document requires --unattended in every brief (section 2.3) and its P0 smoke runs and section 3.1 brief columns omit it, but the document never states that P0 runs are attended; that is a gap in what the P0 runs test, not a pair of stated texts that force a demonstrably wrong build, so the finding needs an added assumption.
evidence: document.md:73 section 2.3 'the exact command line including --unattended'; document.md:79 'run as workers now if the brief uses the stated flags'; document.md:81 3.1 'Brief must pass' column has no --unattended; document.md:158 and 194 P0 runs omit it.

sentence: After P1 an implementer makes auggie-review accept --unattended while its posting default and implied flags are not converted until P2, but the document never says what --unattended does for a gated command in that interim state, so the claim that posting happens needs an assumption about an undefined intermediate state.
evidence: document.md:159 P1 'the --unattended flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)'; document.md:100 auggie-review row 'implies --no-post-pr and --no-remediation-offer'; document.md:160 P2 includes auggie-review; document.md:67 WC-9.

sentence: The rule covers waits 'longer than 5 minutes', so a call of exactly 300 seconds is not addressed, and the document does not say whether a heartbeat can be sent during a tool call; these are unspecified edge cases, so the stated text does not make an implementer build something demonstrably wrong.
evidence: document.md:68 WC-10 'blocks a single tool call for longer than 5 minutes ... split into waits of at most 4 minutes'; document.md:181 step 2 'at least once per 5 minutes'.

sentence: The sentence 'stays a worker candidate only if the user accepts open decision D3' does not say which D3 option counts as acceptance, so an implementer must guess between option (a) and option (b); the ambiguity affects no stated build or acceptance criterion as written.
evidence: document.md:139 'pr-submit stays a worker candidate only if the user accepts open decision D3'; document.md:238-242 D3 options (a) coordinator or person only (recommended) and (b) worker with pre-authorization.

sentence: An implementer who follows R12 and R13 as written builds a restore that overwrites the production database with the selected backup after one confirmation click, with that click as the only check; this is wrong because the stated text itself causes data loss, since every write made after the selected backup is destroyed.
evidence: document.md:23 R12 'A restore overwrites the production database with the selected backup after one confirmation click.'; document.md:24 R13 'The confirmation click is the only check before a restore starts.'

sentence: An implementer who follows R4 builds a writer that never overwrites an existing file in the output directory, and an implementer who follows R7 builds a retry that overwrites the partial file, which is an existing file in that directory; both texts apply to the same retry, so the stated texts contradict and cannot both be satisfied as written, which is wrong under at least one of them.
evidence: document.md:7 R4 'Existing files in the output directory are never overwritten; a numeric suffix is added to the new file name.'; document.md:12 R7 'the retry reuses the file name of the failed attempt and overwrites the partial file.'

sentence: The finding quotes only R1 ('a notification is sent over exactly one channel') and calls its effect a possible user surprise; R1 alone contradicts no other stated text, and a surprise is not a build that is demonstrably wrong under the text, so the finding does not meet the blocking test.
evidence: document.md:4 R1 'A notification is sent over exactly one channel: email, SMS or push.' Not cited by the finding but related: document.md:6 R3 'the notification is not sent over another channel' and document.md:19 R10 'falls back to email' for security alerts; the finding does not raise this tension.
